summary: Portland, Maine-based startup Simply Homes raised $22 million to buy single-family homes in blighted neighborhoods, renovate them, and rent them to very low-income families, the elderly and the disabled, largely via Section-8 vouchers. It uses machine learning to underwrite acquisitions based on housing-authority rent data and says its model was built to withstand high interest rates. The company operates in Pittsburgh and Cleveland and plans to expand to Baltimore and parts of the Midwest.
one_line: Simply Homes raised $22M to use AI-driven underwriting to buy, renovate and rent homes to Section-8 and very low-income tenants.
key_facts: Simply Homes, based in Portland, Maine, recently secured $22 million in funding.
Simply Homes buys single-family homes in blighted neighborhoods, renovates them, and rents them to very low-income families, the elderly and the disabled (or Section-8 voucher holders).
Simply Homes was founded in 2020, bought its first home in January 2023, and was expected to have 108 units by the end of December 2023.
Simply Homes' revenue has grown by more than 50% quarter over quarter since its first-quarter launch.

Over 80% of Simply Homes' tenants are single parents who would need to work an estimated 150 hours a week to afford market-rate rent; under HUD's HCV program they pay no more than 30% of income for rent.
Simply Homes currently operates in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and Cleveland, Ohio, and aims to expand into Baltimore, Maryland, additional Ohio markets and St. Louis, Missouri.
Simply Homes uses an operating company/property company structure; the operating company sources, acquires, renovates and manages properties while the property company holds them long term.
CEO Brian Bagdasarian says Simply Homes underwrote interest rate risk from the start, assuming a worst-case scenario, so high rates have affected it less than first-generation iBuyers.
Simply Homes takes a transaction fee and a 3% ongoing fee to manage the portfolio.
Simply Homes uses housing authority/HUD rent data and machine learning to underwrite acquisitions quickly and accurately.
New capital will partly fund AI-powered virtual analysts that interpret the large amounts of data Simply Homes aggregates for acquisitions.
Gutter Capital and Watchung Capital co-led the $22 million round, with participation from Village Global, Ambush Capital, RavenOne Ventures, Neil Parikh, Gabe Flateman, Luke Sherwin and others.
Gutter Capital's James Gettinger noted average new-construction home size rose from about 1,400 square feet 50 years ago to 2,200 square feet today, leaving few affordable starter homes.
Bagdasarian cites that children moving into lower-poverty neighborhoods can see a 31% increase in lifetime earnings.
